summary: A registered user can reset a forgotten password by requesting a reset link sent to their registered email address. The link is time-limited (expires after 30 minutes) and, once used, the user must set a new password that is at least 12 characters long and different from the previous password. To prevent abuse, the system blocks further reset attempts after three failures within a one-hour window.

business_rules.rule: The system sends a password reset link to the email address if it is registered.
The reset link expires after 30 minutes.
The new password must be at least 12 characters.
The new password must not match the previous password.
After three failed reset attempts within an hour, further attempts are blocked.
Requesting a reset for an unregistered email does not reveal whether the email exists (generic confirmation message shown regardless).
A reset link can only be used once; after successful use it becomes invalid even if not yet expired.
The failed-attempt counter resets once the rolling one-hour window has elapsed since the first counted failure.

scenarios.description: User requests a password reset using a registered email address and receives a reset link.
scenarios.rationale: Primary documented entry point of the feature.

scenarios.description: User clicks a valid, unexpired reset link and successfully sets a new password meeting the length and history rules.
scenarios.rationale: Core success path; failure here blocks the entire feature.

scenarios.description: User logs in successfully with the newly set password after a completed reset.
scenarios.rationale: Confirms the reset actually takes effect end to end.

scenarios.description: User requests a reset with an email address that is not registered in the system.
scenarios.rationale: Verifies handling of unknown accounts without leaking account existence.

scenarios.description: User attempts to use a reset link after it has expired (more than 30 minutes old).
scenarios.rationale: Directly stated expiry rule; must be enforced.

scenarios.description: User attempts to set a new password that matches the previous password.
scenarios.rationale: Directly stated password-history rule.

scenarios.description: User makes a fourth reset attempt within the same hour after three prior failed attempts and is blocked.
scenarios.rationale: Directly stated abuse-prevention rule; security relevant.

scenarios.description: User attempts to reuse an already-successfully-used reset link a second time.
scenarios.rationale: Guards against link replay; based on inferred single-use rule.

scenarios.description: User uses the reset link at exactly the 30-minute expiry boundary.
scenarios.rationale: Exact-boundary check for the stated expiry rule.

scenarios.description: User uses the reset link a few seconds before the 30-minute expiry (still valid).
scenarios.rationale: Just-inside-boundary check complementing SC-9.

scenarios.description: User sets a new password that is exactly 12 characters long (minimum boundary).
scenarios.rationale: Exact minimum-length boundary for the stated password rule.

scenarios.description: User sets a new password that is 11 characters long, one below the minimum.
scenarios.rationale: Just-below-minimum boundary check.

scenarios.description: User's third failed reset attempt within the hour is still allowed (not yet blocked).
scenarios.rationale: Boundary of the three-attempt lockout threshold.

scenarios.description: User's failed-attempt counter resets and a new reset attempt succeeds once the one-hour window has elapsed.
scenarios.rationale: Time-window boundary for the rolling lockout counter.

scenarios.description: User submits the reset request form with an empty email field.
scenarios.rationale: Required-field validation on the request form.

scenarios.description: User submits the reset request form with a malformed email address (invalid format).
scenarios.rationale: Field-format validation on the request form.

scenarios.description: User submits the new-password form with an empty password field.
scenarios.rationale: Required-field validation on the reset completion form.

scenarios.description: User submits a new password containing only whitespace characters.
scenarios.rationale: Edge-case input validation not explicitly covered by length rule alone.

scenarios.description: Reset flow is exercised for an email address containing plus-addressing or mixed case, verifying case-insensitive/canonical email matching.
scenarios.rationale: Data-variation coverage for email formats.

scenarios.description: Reset flow is exercised for two different registered accounts to confirm the failed-attempt lockout counter is tracked per account, not globally.
scenarios.rationale: Data/state variation ensuring lockout isolation between users.

scenarios.description: Reset link expiry is verified consistently across requests issued in different time zones/locales.
scenarios.rationale: Data variation ensuring expiry timing is computed on a consistent (e.g. server/UTC) clock.

functional: Successful password change via valid link
Login with new password after reset

assumptions: REQ-042 has an explicit ID in the source document, so it is used as requirement_reference.
Assumed the system shows a generic confirmation message for reset requests regardless of whether the email is registered, to avoid account enumeration; the requirement does not state this.
Assumed a reset link is single-use and becomes invalid immediately after a successful password change, even if the 30-minute window has not elapsed; the requirement does not state this explicitly.

Assumed the three-failed-attempt lockout counter is scoped per account and resets on a rolling one-hour basis from the first failure; the requirement does not specify the counter's scope or exact reset mechanics.
Assumed no additional password complexity rules (character classes, symbols) apply beyond the stated 12-character minimum and the previous-password-mismatch rule.
Assumed the reset request form has a single email field and the reset completion form has a single new-password field, with no explicit confirm-password field mentioned in the requirement.
risks: The requirement is silent on the lockout duration and the exact mechanism/timing for un-blocking a user after three failed attempts, which could lead to inconsistent implementation.
The requirement is silent on whether reset requests reveal account existence (email enumeration), a potential security concern if not addressed deliberately.
The requirement is silent on whether a reset link is single-use, leaving replay behavior open to interpretation.
The requirement is silent on password complexity beyond minimum length, so validation scenarios beyond length/history are based on inference rather than stated rules.
No instruction-like or prompt-injection content was found in the requirement text; none was ignored.
